entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12456"/><div sID="gen22882" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12456"/><hi type="bold">2. darkness ... gloominess ... clouds ... thick darkness--</hi>accumulation of synonyms, to intensify the picture of calamity (<reference osisRef="Isa.8.22">Is 8:22</reference>). Appropriate here, as the swarms of locusts intercepting the sunlight suggested darkness as a fit image of the coming visitation.<div eID="gen22882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22883" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people--</hi>Substitute a comma for a colon after mountains: As the morning light spreads itself over the mountains, so a people numerous [Maurer] and strong shall spread themselves. The suddenness of the rising of the morning light, which gilds the mountain tops first, is less probably thought by others to be the point of comparison to the sudden inroad of the foe. Maurer refers it to the yellow splendor which arises from the reflection of the sunlight on the wings of the immense hosts of locusts as they approach. This is likely; understanding, however, that the locusts are only the symbols of human foes. The immense Assyrian host of invaders under Sennacherib (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.37.36">Is 37:36</reference>) destroyed by God (<reference osisRef="Joel.2.18">Joe 2:18</reference>, 20, 21), may be the primary objects of the prophecy; but ultimately the last antichristian confederacy, destroyed by special divine interposition, is meant (see on <reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">Joe 3:2</reference>).<div eID="gen22883" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22884" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">there hath not been ever the like--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Joel.1.2">Joe 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.10.14">Ex 10:14</reference>). <div eID="gen22884" type="x-p"/>

This is likely; understanding, however, that the locusts are only the symbols of human foes. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12458"/><div sID="gen22888" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12458"/><hi type="bold">4. appearance ... of horses--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Rev.9.7">Re 9:7</reference>). Not literal, but figurative locusts. The fifth trumpet, or first woe, in the parallel passage (<reference osisRef="Rev.9.1-Rev.9.11">Re 9:1-11</reference>), cannot be literal: for in <reference osisRef="Rev.9.11">Re 9:11</reference> it is said, "they had a king over them, the angel of the bottomless pit"--in the Hebrew, Abaddon ("destroyer"), but in the Greek, Apollyon--and (<reference osisRef="Rev.9.7">Re 9:7</reference>) "on their heads were as it were crowns like gold, and their faces were as the faces of men." Compare <reference osisRef="Joel.2.11">Joe 2:11</reference>, "the day of the Lord ... great and very terrible"; implying their ultimate reference to be connected with Messiah's second coming in judgment. The locust's head is so like that of a horse that the Italians call it cavalette. Compare <reference osisRef="Job.39.20">Job 39:20</reference>, "the horse ... as the grasshopper," or locust.<div eID="gen22888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22889" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">run--</hi>The locust bounds, not unlike the horse's gallop, raising and letting down together the two front feet. <div eID="gen22889" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12471"/><div sID="gen22918" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12471"/><hi type="bold">17. between the porch and ... altar--</hi>the porch of Solomon's temple on the east (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.6.3">1Ki 6:3</reference>); the altar of burnt offerings in the court of the priests, before the porch (<reference osisRef="2Chr.8.12">2Ch 8:12</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.8.16">Eze 8:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.23.35">Mt 23:35</reference>). The suppliants thus were to stand with their backs to the altar on which they had nothing to offer, their faces towards the place of the Shekinah presence.<div eID="gen22918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22919" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heathen should rule over them--</hi>This shows that not locusts, but human foes, are intended. The Margin translation, "use a byword against them," is not supported by the Hebrew.<div eID="gen22919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22920" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wherefore should they say ... Where is their God?--</hi>that is, do not for thine own honor's sake, let the heathen sneer at the God of Israel, as unable to save His people (<reference osisRef="Ps.79.10">Psa 79:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.115.2">115:2</reference>). <div eID="gen22920" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 17. between the porch and ... altar-- the porch of Solomon's temple on the east ( 1Ki 6:3 ); the altar of burnt offerings in the court of the priests, before the porch ( 2Ch 8:12 ; compare Eze 8:16 ; Mt 23:35 ). The suppliants thus were to stand with their backs to the altar on which they had nothing to offer, their faces towards the place of the Shekinah presence. heathen should rule over them-- This shows that not locusts, but human foes, are intended. The Margin translation, "use a byword against them," is not supported by the Hebrew. wherefore should they say ... Where is their God?-- that is, do not for thine own honor's sake, let the heathen sneer at the God of Israel, as unable to save His people ( Psa 79:10 ; 115:2 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12474"/><div sID="gen22924" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12474"/><hi type="bold">20. the northern army--</hi>The Hebrew expresses that the north in relation to Palestine is not merely the quarter whence the invader comes, but is his native land, "the Northlander"; namely, the Assyrian or Babylonian (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.1.14">Jr 1:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.15">15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.2.13">Zep 2:13</reference>). The locust's native country is not the north, but the south, the deserts of Arabia, Egypt, and Libya. Assyria and Babylon are the type and forerunner of all Israel's foes (Rome, and the final Antichrist), from whom God will at last deliver His people, as He did from Sennacherib (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.19.35">2Ki 19:35</reference>).<div eID="gen22924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22925" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">face ... hinder part--</hi>more applicable to a human army's van and rear, than to locusts. The northern invaders are to be dispersed in every other direction but that from which they had come: "a land barren and desolate," that is, Arabia-Deserta: "the eastern (or front) sea," that is, the Dead Sea: "the utmost (or hinder) sea," that is, the Mediterranean. In front and behind mean east and west; as, in marking the quarters of the world, they faced the east, which was therefore "in front"; the west was behind them; the south was on their right, and the north on their left.<div eID="gen22925" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22926" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stink--</hi>metaphor from locusts, which perish when blown by a storm into the sea or the desert, and emit from their putrefying bodies such a stench as often breeds a pestilence.<div eID="gen22926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22927" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">because he hath done great things--</hi>that is, because the invader hath haughtily magnified himself in his doings. Compare as to Sennacherib, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.19.11-2Kgs.13.22">2Ki 19:11-13, 22</reference>, 28. This is quite inapplicable to the locusts, who merely seek food, not self-glorification, in invading a country. <div eID="gen22927" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12481"/><div sID="gen22937" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12481"/><hi type="bold">27. know that I am in the midst of Israel--</hi>As in the Old Testament dispensation God was present by the Shekinah, so in the New Testament first, for a brief time by the Word made flesh dwelling among us (<reference osisRef="John.1.14">Joh 1:14</reference>), and to the close of this dispensation by the Holy Spirit in the Church (<reference osisRef="Matt.28.20">Mt 28:20</reference>), and probably in a more perceptible manner with Israel when restored (<reference osisRef="Ezek.37.26-Ezek.37.28">Eze 37:26-28</reference>).<div eID="gen22937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22938" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">never be ashamed--</hi>not an unmeaning repetition from <reference osisRef="Joel.2.26">Joe 2:26</reference>. The twice-asserted truth enforces its unfailing certainty. As the "shame" in <reference osisRef="Joel.2.26">Joe 2:26</reference> refers to temporal blessings, so in this verse it refers to the spiritual blessings flowing from the presence of God with His people (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.3.16">Jr 3:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.3.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.21.3">Re 21:3</reference>). <div eID="gen22938" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 27. know that I am in the midst of Israel-- As in the Old Testament dispensation God was present by the Shekinah, so in the New Testament first, for a brief time by the Word made flesh dwelling among us ( Joh 1:14 ), and to the close of this dispensation by the Holy Spirit in the Church ( Mt 28:20 ), and probably in a more perceptible manner with Israel when restored ( Eze 37:26-28 ). never be ashamed-- not an unmeaning repetition from Joe 2:26 . The twice-asserted truth enforces its unfailing certainty. As the "shame" in Joe 2:26 refers to temporal blessings, so in this verse it refers to the spiritual blessings flowing from the presence of God with His people (compare Jr 3:16 , 17 ; Re 21:3 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12482"/><div sID="gen22939" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12482"/><hi type="bold">28. afterward--</hi>"in the last days" (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.2">Is 2:2</reference>) under Messiah after the invasion and deliverance of Israel from the northern army. Having heretofore stated the outward blessings, he now raises their minds to the expectation of extraordinary spiritual blessings, which constitute the true restoration of God's people (<reference osisRef="Isa.44.3">Is 44:3</reference>). Fulfilled in earnest (<reference osisRef="Acts.2.17">Ac 2:17</reference>) on Pentecost; among the Jews and the subsequent election of a people among the Gentiles; hereafter more fully at the restoration of Israel (<reference osisRef="Isa.54.13">Is 54:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.9">Jr 31:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.31.34">34</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.29">Eze 39:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">Zec 12:10</reference>) and the consequent conversion of the whole world (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.2">Is 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.11.9">11:9</reference>; 66:18-23; <reference osisRef="Mic.5.7">Mi 5:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.11.12">Ro 11:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.11.15">15</reference>). As the Jews have been the seedmen of the elect Church gathered out of Jews and Gentiles, the first Gospel preachers being Jews from Jerusalem, so they shall be the harvest men of the coming world-wide Church, to be set up at Messiah's appearing. That the promise is not restricted to the first Pentecost appears from Peter's own words: "The promise is (not only) unto you and to your children, (but also) to all that are afar off (both in space and in time), even as many as the Lord our God shall call" (<reference osisRef="Acts.2.39">Ac 2:39</reference>). So here "upon all flesh."<div eID="gen22939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22940" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will pour out--</hi>under the new covenant: not merely, let fall drops, as under the Old Testament (<reference osisRef="John.7.39">Joh 7:39</reference>).<div eID="gen22940" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22941" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my spirit--</hi>the Spirit "proceeding from the Father and the Son," and at the same time one with the Father and the Son (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.11.2">Is 11:2</reference>).<div eID="gen22941" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22942" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sons ... daughters ... old ... young--</hi>not merely on a privileged few (<reference osisRef="Num.11.29">Nu 11:29</reference>) as the prophets of the Old Testament, but men of all ages and ranks. See <reference osisRef="Acts.21.9">Ac 21:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.11.5">1Co 11:5</reference>, as to "daughters," that is, women, prophesying.<div eID="gen22942" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22943" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dreams ... visions--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Acts.9.10">Ac 9:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.16.9">16:9</reference>). The "dreams" are attributed to the "old men," as more in accordance with their years; "visions" to the "young men," as adapted to their more lively minds. The three modes whereby God revealed His will under the Old Testament (<reference osisRef="Num.12.6">Nu 12:6</reference>), "prophecy, dreams, and visions," are here made the symbol of the full manifestation of Himself to all His people, not only in miraculous gifts to some, but by His indwelling Spirit to all in the New Testament (<reference osisRef="John.14.21">Joh 14:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="John.14.23">23</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.15.15">15:15</reference>). In <reference osisRef="Acts.16.9">Ac 16:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.18.9">18:9</reference>, the term used is "vision," though in the night, not a dream. No other dream is mentioned in the New Testament save those given to Joseph in the very beginning of the New Testament, before the full Gospel had come; and to the wife of Pilate, a Gentile (<reference osisRef="Matt.1.20">Mt 1:20</reference>; 2:13; 27:19). "Prophesying" in the New Testament is applied to all speaking under the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit, and not merely to foretelling events. All true Christians are "priests" and "ministers" of our God (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.6">Is 61:6</reference>), and have the Spirit (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.26">Eze 36:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.27">27</reference>). Besides this, probably, a special gift of prophecy and miracle-working is to be given at or before Messiah's coming again. <div eID="gen22943" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 28. afterward-- "in the last days" ( Is 2:2 ) under Messiah after the invasion and deliverance of Israel from the northern army. Fulfilled in earnest ( Ac 2:17 ) on Pentecost; among the Jews and the subsequent election of a people among the Gentiles; hereafter more fully at the restoration of Israel ( Is 54:13 ; Jr 31:9 , 34 ; Eze 39:29 ; Zec 12:10 ) and the consequent conversion of the whole world ( Is 2:2 ; 11:9 ; 66:18-23; Mi 5:7 ; Ro 11:12 , 15 ). And also--</hi>"And even." The very slaves by becoming the Lord's servants are His freemen (<reference osisRef="1Cor.7.22">1Co 7:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.3.28">Ga 3:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.3.11">Col 3:11</reference>; Phm 16). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12484"/><div sID="gen22945" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12484"/>30-31. As Messiah's manifestation is full of joy to believers, so it has an aspect of wrath to unbelievers, which is represented here. Thus when the Jews received Him not in His coming of grace, He came in judgment on Jerusalem. Physical prodigies, massacres, and conflagrations preceded its destruction [Josephus, Wars of the Jews]. To these the language here may allude; but the figures chiefly symbolize political revolutions and changes in the ruling powers of the world, prognosticated by previous disasters (<reference osisRef="Amos.8.9">Am 8:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.24.29">Mt 24:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.21.25-Luke.21.27">Lu 21:25-27</reference>), and convulsions such as preceded the overthrow of the Jewish polity. Such shall probably occur in a more appalling degree before the final destruction of the ungodly world ("the great and terrible day of Jehovah," compare Mal 4:5), of which Jerusalem's overthrow is the type and earnest. <div eID="gen22945" type="x-p"/>

Lord--</hi>Hebrew, Jehovah.
